item.title: Space Force Expands Use Of Commercial Satellites To Track Electronic Interference
item.description: WASHINGTON — The U.S. Space Force is expanding the use of commercial satellites to detect and locate GPS jamming and other electronic interference, turning what began as an experiment into a standing global operation.

item.title: Rocket Lab Continues High Electron Cadence With Synspective Launch
item.description: PARIS — Rocket Lab launched a radar-imaging satellite for Japanese company Synspective on Sept. 18 on the fifth flight of its Electron rocket in a month and a half.

item.title: Sedaro gets $45 million in Space Force funding to expand mission analysis software
item.description: WASHINGTON — Space software company Sedaro will receive up to $45 million in government funding to expand a platform that helps the U.S. Space Force analyze how different satellites, sensors and other capabilities perform together.

item.title: Nasa Adds Three Iss Missions To Spacex Crew Dragon Contract
item.description: PARIS — NASA has proceeded with plans to purchase three additional SpaceX Crew Dragon missions to the International Space Station, although the spacecraft’s long-term future remains uncertain.

item.title: Final Viasat 3 Enters Service As Ses Wraps Up O3B Mpower Launch Campaign
item.description: TAMPA, Fla. — The third and final terabit-class ViaSat-3 broadband satellite has entered service over the Americas, the U.S. operator announced Sept. 17, days after SpaceX launched the final three spacecraft for Luxembourg-based SES’ O3b mPower network.

item.description: TAMPA, Fla. — There are early signs of a resurgence in communications satellites destined for commercial customers in geostationary orbit (GEO), following years of being overshadowed by massive broadband constellations flying much closer to Earth.

item.title: Aschbacher Upbeat About Winning Support For A European Human Spaceflight Program
item.description: PARIS — The head of the European Space Agency is optimistic that member states will back plans to pursue human spaceflight and other key programs at a critical December meeting.

item.title: Astra Projecting Early 2027 For The Introduction Of Rocket 4 0
item.description: PARIS — Astra is now planning a first launch of its Rocket 4.0 vehicle in early 2027 as it aims to reenter a market increasingly desperate for launch capacity.

item.title: Satellite Operators Weigh Spacex Ipo Impact As Dust Settles
item.description: TAMPA, Fla. — SpaceX’s industry-shaking IPO more than three months ago continues to have far-reaching and mixed effects for other satellite broadband operators.

item.title: Jamming created a resilience market. The space industry is losing it to the ground.
item.description: In the first quarter of this year, roughly 978,000 maritime GPS jamming events were recorded worldwide. Ninety-eight percent of them happened in one place: the Middle East Gulf. It is the largest single-quarter concentration of maritime jamming ever recorded, and more than 1,100 vessels in the region were affected.

item.title: Eight African nations signed the Artemis Accords. Now give them a path to the moon.
item.description: A year and a half ago, we took to SpaceNews to plead our case: If the United States teamed up with African nations in space, everyone would win. Washington would deepen relationships across a fast-changing continent while African partners could use space technology to tackle critical problems like food insecurity, climate resilience and digital isolation.
